spec.description: Subscribe to reference data for all active assets and tradeable pairs -- symbol identifiers, precisions, and trading parameters and rules.

parameters.title: InstrumentParams
parameters.description: Parameters for an `instrument` channel subscription. Unlike the other market-data channels, this one takes no `symbol` list -- it always streams the full reference data set.

execution_venue.description: The execution venue for the instrument channel.

include_tokenized_assets.description: If `true`, include xStocks in the response; otherwise include crypto spot pairs only.

payload.title: InstrumentMessage
payload.description: An `instrument` channel push. Unlike the other market-data channels, `data` is a single object (an `{assets, pairs}` reference-data set), not an array of per-symbol entries.

channel.description: The channel this push belongs to.

type.description: Whether this push is the initial snapshot or an incremental update.

data.title: InstrumentData
data.description: The reference-data set carried by this push.

precision.description: Maximum precision for asset ledger, balances.

collateral_value.description: Valuation as margin collateral, if applicable.

margin_rate.description: Interest rate to borrow the asset.

multiplier.description: Multiplier of the tokenised asset -- fixed conversion rate of the token.

pairs.description: Tradeable pairs included in this push.

items.title: InstrumentPair
items.description: Reference data for one tradeable pair.

symbol.description: The symbol of the currency pair, e.g. `"BTC/USD"`.

base.description: Asset identifier of the base currency.

quote.description: Asset identifier of the quote currency.

qty_precision.description: Maximum precision used for order quantities.

qty_increment.description: Minimum quantity increment for new orders.

qty_min.description: Minimum quantity, in base currency, for new orders.

price_precision.description: Maximum precision used for order prices.

price_increment.description: Minimum price increment for new orders.

cost_precision.description: Maximum precision used for cost prices.

cost_min.description: Minimum cost (price * qty) for new orders.

has_index.description: Whether the pair has an index available, e.g. for stop-loss triggers.

marginable.description: Whether the pair can be traded on margin.

margin_initial.description: Initial margin requirement, in percent. Present on marginable pairs only.

position_limit_long.description: Limit for long positions. Present on marginable pairs only.

position_limit_short.description: Limit for short positions. Present on marginable pairs only.

ws_display_price_precision.description: Recommended display precision for prices in WebSocket feeds.

tick_size.description: Minimum price increment for new orders. Deprecated -- use `price_increment`.

notes: `data` is a single object (`{assets, pairs}`), not an array, unlike every other market-data channel in this batch -- kept as-is rather than force-fit into the `data: array` pattern the others share. No field on this page carries a `required` tag at all; `id` (assets) and `symbol` (pairs) are marked required here as the sole always-present identifiers evidenced by every worked example (snapshot and update alike), everything else is `NotRequired` since the update example shows a partial asset entry and several pair fields are explicitly documented as conditional ('On marginable pairs only'). Note the venue is internally inconsistent on enum casing between this endpoint and `status`: asset `status` uses no-underscore values (`workinprogress`) while pair `status` and the `status` channel's `system` both use underscored values (`work_in_progress`, `cancel_only`) -- both are transcribed verbatim from the docs, not normalized.
